headline: Freight demand strength drives a sharp earnings acceleration
summary_short: J.B. Hunt's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 19% year-over-year to $3.50 billion and diluted EPS climbed 45% to $1.91, as operating income jumped 32% to $259.5 million on broad-based freight-demand strength led by Intermodal.
summary_long: Growth was broad-based: Intermodal revenue rose 22% and operating income 58% on strong Eastern-network demand and dray productivity; Dedicated grew 9% on productivity; ICS swung to a small profit from a loss on higher rates and volume. Final Mile revenue fell 6% and Truckload posted a small operating loss on higher purchased-transportation costs. Consolidated operating income rose 32% on cost discipline and lower medical claims; a 21% drop in net interest expense and a lower 25.4% tax rate pushed EPS up 45%, outpacing operating-income growth. Cash fell to $4.2 million (from $50.9 million a year ago) as the company paid down debt to $1.15 billion and repurchased $98 million of stock. Management now expects a 24.0%-24.5% FY2026 tax rate.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by higher Intermodal, ICS and Truckload load volumes and revenue per load, plus Dedicated productivity gains; partly offset by a 14% Final Mile stop decline.
Gain driven by higher revenue, productivity improvements, structural cost removal, and lower medical claims and facility costs, partly offset by higher purchased-transportation and equipment expense.
EPS grew faster than operating income on a 21% drop in net interest expense, a lower 25.4% effective tax rate (vs 26.9%), and a smaller diluted share count from buybacks.
Cash fell to $4.2 million from $50.9 million a year ago as the company paid down debt to $1.15 billion (from $1.72 billion) and repurchased $98 million of stock in the quarter.
Debt declined as the company continued paying down debt instruments outstanding; six-month net capex fell to $144.9 million from $399.1 million a year earlier, freeing cash for debt reduction.
Share count fell on continued buybacks: about $98 million of stock repurchased this quarter, out of a $791 million remaining authorization.

Intermodal, the largest segment, led results: revenue +22% and operating income +58% on strong Eastern-network volume growth, dray-network productivity, and lower container storage/empty-repositioning costs.
